A co-expression module is a group of proteins whose abundances rise and fall together across
biopsies. WGCNA (Langfelder and Horvath 2008) finds them, and each module is then summarised by
its eigengene: one number per biopsy that follows the module's shared pattern. Later steps test
eigengenes instead of hundreds of single proteins. Module construction never sees a group label or
a phenotype.

## Packages

```{r}
#| label: packages
#| message: false
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)
library(WGCNA)
source(here("00_Setup", "Shared_functions", "workbooks.R"))
disableWGCNAThreads()
inputs <- c(corrected = "01_Processing/03_Blood_Correction/c_data/proteins_corrected.rds")
paths <- vapply(inputs, here, character(1))
stopifnot(file.exists(paths))
```

## Input

limpa's complete matrix with each protein's blood slope removed from its observed values
(`03_Blood_Correction`). WGCNA takes no covariate and no missing values, so this is the matrix it
can use.

```{r}
#| label: input
corrected <- readRDS(paths[["corrected"]])
abund <- corrected$E
meta <- as_tibble(corrected$targets) |>
  select(sample_id, subject, group, timepoint)
stopifnot(identical(colnames(abund), meta$sample_id))
dim(abund)
count(count(meta, subject, name = "biopsies"), biopsies, name = "people")
```

## Define modules on within-person variation

WGCNA treats every biopsy as an independent sample. These 48 biopsies come from 16 people at three
time points each, and person identity drives the leading components of the abundance matrix. Left
alone, modules would mostly group proteins that differ between people. So the modules are defined
on person-centred abundance: each protein's value minus that person's mean over their three
biopsies.

```{r}
#| label: centre
centred <- t(apply(abund, 1, \(x) x - ave(x, meta$subject)))
expr <- t(centred)
one <- meta$sample_id[meta$subject == meta$subject[1]]
rbind(raw = round(abund[1, one], 2), centred = round(centred[1, one], 2))
dim(expr)
```

## Soft power

WGCNA turns each pair's correlation into a connection strength by raising it to a power (the soft
power): higher powers keep strong links and shrink weak ones. The usual rule takes the lowest power
whose network looks scale-free (a few proteins carry many connections, most carry few) by a fit R²
of at least 0.85. Here that rule picks a power so high that the network is almost empty, so the
power is set by hand:

- The fit first reaches 0.85 at power 19, where a protein has on average 1.3 connections and 73%
  of proteins fit no module. Zhang and Horvath (2005) warn that pushing the fit up this way leaves
  networks with very few connections, too little to find modules in.
- On pure noise of the same shape (2,059 features, 48 biopsies, person-centred) the fit also climbs
  with power (R² 0.51 at power 19) while connectivity falls towards zero, so reaching 0.85 at a
  high power is weak evidence of structure.
- 12 is the WGCNA FAQ's power for signed networks with more than 40 samples, the value its author
  gives when the rule is met only at a higher power (support.bioconductor.org/p/93649,
  /p/87069, /p/124844).
- 10 is used here, with modules merged at eigengene correlation 0.75: in the settings screen below
  this pair gives the modules that best re-form when one person is left out (decisions log,
  2026-10-28). The module QC compares powers 8, 12 and 14.

Two settings depart from the package defaults, both recommended in the WGCNA FAQ:

- a signed network, so proteins that move in opposite directions are not linked;
- biweight midcorrelation (bicor), a correlation that down-weights outlying values, with
  `maxPOutliers = 0.05` (the default of 1 switches that guard off). `pearsonFallback` uses an
  ordinary correlation for a protein with zero spread.

```{r}
#| label: soft-power
bicor_args <- list(corType = "bicor", maxPOutliers = 0.05, pearsonFallback = "individual")
sft <- pickSoftThreshold(expr,
  powerVector = 1:22, networkType = "signed", corFnc = "bicor",
  corOptions = list(maxPOutliers = 0.05, pearsonFallback = "individual"), verbose = 0
)
power <- 10L
fit_indices <- as_tibble(sft$fitIndices) |>
  mutate(signed_r2 = -sign(slope) * SFT.R.sq, chosen = Power == power)
filter(fit_indices, Power %in% c(10, 12, 14, 19)) |>
  select(Power, signed_r2, mean.k., chosen)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-soft-power
#| fig-cap: "Connectivity and signed scale-free fit by soft power; dashed 0.85, red chosen."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 3.5
fit_indices |>
  select(Power, `signed scale-free R2` = signed_r2, `mean connectivity` = mean.k.) |>
  pivot_longer(-Power) |>
  ggplot(aes(Power, value)) +
  geom_line(colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = Power == power), size = 2) +
  geom_hline(
    data = tibble(name = "signed scale-free R2", y = 0.85), aes(yintercept = y),
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey30", `TRUE` = "#B2182B"), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "soft power", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10)
```

## Modules

`blockwiseModules()` builds the network, measures how many neighbours each pair shares (the
topological overlap, TOM), clusters proteins on it, and merges modules whose eigengenes correlate
above 0.75 (`mergeCutHeight = 0.25`, the value YvO used). Proteins that fit no module go to `grey`.
Settings that are not package defaults: `minModuleSize = 30` and `maxBlockSize = 2500`, which
keeps all `r nrow(abund)` proteins in one block; the settings screen below compares them with
finer splits. `randomSeed` seeds the clustering inside the function; a `set.seed()` outside it
would be overridden. `build_at()` runs the whole construction, so the QC and the screen repeat it
unchanged.

```{r}
#| label: modules
build_at <- function(p, x = expr, deep_split = 2, min_size = 30, merge = 0.25) {
  set_names(do.call(blockwiseModules, c(
    list(x,
      power = p, networkType = "signed", TOMType = "signed", deepSplit = deep_split,
      minModuleSize = min_size, mergeCutHeight = merge, pamStage = TRUE,
      pamRespectsDendro = TRUE, maxBlockSize = 2500, numericLabels = FALSE, randomSeed = 54321,
      verbose = 0
    ),
    bicor_args
  ))$colors, colnames(x))
}
colours <- build_at(power)
sort(table(colours), decreasing = TRUE)
```

At power `r power` a protein has on average `r round(fit_indices$mean.k.[fit_indices$chosen], 1)`
connections and `r round(100 * mean(colours == "grey"))`% of proteins fit no module.

## Module QC: how much the power matters

The same construction at powers 8, 12 and 14, compared with power 10 by WGCNA's `overlapTable()`:
for each power-10 module, the share of its proteins that land in its best-matching module at the
other power. A module that keeps most of its proteins at 8 and 12 does not depend on the exact
power.

```{r}
#| label: module-qc
module_qc <- map(set_names(c(8, 12, 14)), \(p) {
  other <- build_at(p)
  overlap <- overlapTable(colours, other)$countTable
  overlap <- overlap[rownames(overlap) != "grey", colnames(overlap) != "grey", drop = FALSE]
  tibble(
    module = rownames(overlap), n_proteins = as.vector(table(colours)[rownames(overlap)]),
    kept_share = apply(overlap, 1, max) / n_proteins,
    n_modules_other = n_distinct(other[other != "grey"]), grey_other = sum(other == "grey")
  )
}) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "power_other")
module_qc |>
  summarise(
    modules = first(n_modules_other), grey = first(grey_other),
    median_kept = round(median(kept_share), 2), .by = power_other
  )
```

## Settings screen: do modules re-form without one person?

With 16 people, a module that one person's three biopsies make or break is not a property of
muscle. The screen builds each of 32 settings on everyone and 16 more times with one person left
out: power 10 or 12, merge height 0.15 or 0.25, deepSplit 2 or 3, minimum size 20 or 30, and all
proteins or only those observed in at least 36 of 48 biopsies. A full-data module re-forms in a
fold when its best-matching fold module shares at least half its proteins (Jaccard >= 0.5, the YvO
rule); its stability is the median of those best matches over the 16 folds. Finer splits
(deepSplit 3, minimum 20) re-form less often, so the modules here are kept coarse. A scratch run
with uncentred input gave similar trade-offs.

```{r}
#| label: settings-screen
observed <- rowSums(corrected$other$n.observations > 0)
members <- \(colours) split(names(colours), colours)[setdiff(unique(colours), "grey")]
best_jaccard <- function(full, fold) {
  map_dbl(full, \(m) max(map_dbl(fold, \(f) length(intersect(m, f)) / length(union(m, f))), 0))
}
stability_of <- function(p, x = expr, ...) {
  full <- members(build_at(p, x, ...))
  folds <- map(unique(meta$subject), \(s) members(build_at(p, x[meta$subject != s, ], ...)))
  jaccard <- do.call(cbind, map(folds, \(f) best_jaccard(full, f)))
  tibble(
    module = names(full), n_proteins = lengths(full), stability = apply(jaccard, 1, median),
    reform_share = rowMeans(jaccard >= 0.5)
  )
}
screen_grid <- expand_grid(
  proteins = c("all", "observed_36"), power = c(10, 12), merge = c(0.15, 0.25),
  deep_split = 2:3, min_size = c(20, 30)
)
settings_screen <- parallel::mclapply(seq_len(nrow(screen_grid)), \(g) {
  s <- screen_grid[g, ]
  x <- if (s$proteins == "all") expr else expr[, observed >= 36]
  stability_of(s$power, x, deep_split = s$deep_split, min_size = s$min_size, merge = s$merge) |>
    summarise(
      n_modules = n(), share_in_modules = sum(n_proteins) / ncol(x),
      median_stability = median(stability), n_reforming = sum(stability >= 0.5)
    ) |>
    bind_cols(s, n_tested = ncol(x))
}, mc.cores = max(1, parallel::detectCores() - 1)) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  relocate(proteins, power, merge, deep_split, min_size, n_tested) |>
  mutate(
    chosen = proteins == "all" & power == 10 & merge == 0.25 & deep_split == 2 & min_size == 30
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(median_stability))
stopifnot(sum(settings_screen$chosen) == 1)
head(settings_screen, 8)
```

The modules used here, one by one:

```{r}
#| label: module-stability
module_stability <- stability_of(power)
stopifnot(setequal(module_stability$module, setdiff(unique(colours), "grey")))
arrange(module_stability, desc(stability))
```

## Eigengenes and membership

The eigengene is the first principal component of a module's proteins, scored here on the
uncentred matrix so that differences between people, and so between HR and LR, stay testable.
`moduleEigengenes()` flips each eigengene's sign to follow the module's average abundance (package
default).

```{r}
#| label: eigengenes
me <- moduleEigengenes(t(abund), colors = colours, excludeGrey = TRUE)$eigengenes
rownames(me) <- colnames(abund)
eigengenes <- t(as.matrix(me))
rownames(eigengenes) <- sub("^ME", "", rownames(eigengenes))
dim(eigengenes)
round(eigengenes[1:3, 1:4], 3)
```

A protein's kME is its correlation with its module's eigengene: near 1 means it follows the module
closely. kME is read on the person-centred data that defined the modules, because on uncentred
data the differences between people dilute it. The gene is the first symbol limpa gives the
protein.

```{r}
#| label: kme
centred_me <- moduleEigengenes(expr, colors = colours, excludeGrey = TRUE)$eigengenes
kme <- signedKME(expr, centred_me,
  corFnc = "bicor", corOptions = "maxPOutliers = 0.05, pearsonFallback = 'individual'"
)
colnames(kme) <- sub("^kME", "", colnames(kme))
membership <- tibble(
  uniprot_id = names(colours),
  gene = sub(";.*", "", corrected$genes[names(colours), "Genes"]),
  module = unname(colours)
) |>
  mutate(kme = map2_dbl(uniprot_id, module, \(id, m) if (m == "grey") NA_real_ else kme[id, m]))
membership |>
  filter(module != "grey") |>
  slice_max(kme, n = 2, by = module) |>
  arrange(module) |>
  head(6)
```

## How much each eigengene still depends on the person

The intraclass correlation (ICC) is the share of an eigengene's variance that lies between people
rather than between one person's biopsies, from a mixed model with time point fitted (lme4,
`eigengene ~ timepoint + (1 | subject)`), so time effects do not count as noise.

```{r}
#| label: icc
eigengene_long <- as_tibble(t(eigengenes), rownames = "sample_id") |>
  pivot_longer(-sample_id, names_to = "module", values_to = "eigengene") |>
  left_join(meta, by = "sample_id")
subject_icc <- eigengene_long |>
  summarise(
    icc = {
      v <- as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(suppressMessages(
        lme4::lmer(eigengene ~ timepoint + (1 | subject))
      )))$vcov
      v[1] / (v[1] + v[2])
    },
    .by = module
  )
module_summary <- count(filter(membership, module != "grey"), module, name = "n_proteins") |>
  left_join(subject_icc, by = "module") |>
  arrange(desc(n_proteins))
module_summary
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-sizes
#| fig-cap: "Proteins per module, labelled with the eigengene's person ICC."
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4.5
module_colours <- set_names(module_summary$module, module_summary$module)
module_summary |>
  mutate(module = factor(module, levels = rev(module))) |>
  ggplot(aes(n_proteins, module, fill = module)) +
  geom_col(colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("ICC %.2f", icc)), hjust = -0.15, size = 3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = module_colours, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.2))) +
  labs(x = "proteins", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-trajectories
#| fig-cap: "Eigengene per biopsy. Thin lines: one person. Thick line and range: group mean ± SE."
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6
trajectory <- eigengene_long |>
  summarise(
    mean = mean(eigengene), se = sd(eigengene) / sqrt(n()),
    .by = c(module, group, timepoint)
  )
ggplot(trajectory, aes(timepoint, mean, colour = group, group = group)) +
  geom_line(
    data = eigengene_long, aes(y = eigengene, group = subject),
    alpha = 0.2, linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = mean - se, ymax = mean + se), size = 0.25) +
  facet_wrap(~ factor(module, levels = module_summary$module)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(HR = "#2166AC", LR = "#B2182B"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "eigengene") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10)
```

## Validation

```{r}
#| label: validate
stopifnot(
  identical(colnames(eigengenes), meta$sample_id),
  setequal(rownames(eigengenes), setdiff(unique(colours), "grey")),
  all(abs(membership$kme[membership$module != "grey"]) <= 1),
  sum(module_summary$n_proteins) + sum(colours == "grey") == nrow(abund),
  !anyNA(membership$gene)
)
```

## Summary

```{r}
#| label: summary
at_power <- filter(fit_indices, Power == power)
select(at_power, Power, signed_r2, mean.k.)
```

Soft power `r power` (signed R² `r round(at_power$signed_r2, 3)`, mean connectivity
`r round(at_power$mean.k., 1)`). `r nrow(eigengenes)` modules of `r min(module_summary$n_proteins)`
to `r max(module_summary$n_proteins)` proteins; `r sum(colours == "grey")` of `r length(colours)`
proteins fit no module. Module colours are labels only and change if `01_Processing` is rebuilt.

## Save

`modules.rds` holds the eigengenes (module by biopsy), the membership with kME, the biopsy table
(`meta`) and the module summary; every module-level step reads it.

```{r}
#| label: save
out <- here("01_Processing", "06_Module_Building", "c_data")
dir.create(out, showWarnings = FALSE)
saveRDS(
  list(
    eigengenes = eigengenes, membership = membership, meta = meta, module_summary = module_summary
  ),
  file.path(out, "modules.rds"),
  compress = "xz"
)
sheets <- list(
  module_summary = module_summary, membership = membership,
  eigengenes = as_tibble(t(eigengenes), rownames = "sample_id"),
  soft_threshold = fit_indices, module_qc = module_qc, settings_screen = settings_screen,
  module_stability = module_stability
)
holds <- c(
  "Proteins per module and the subject ICC of its eigengene.",
  "Every protein's module and its kME in that module.",
  "Module eigengene per biopsy, scored on uncentred abundance.",
  "pickSoftThreshold fit indices per power; chosen marks the power used (10).",
  "Per power-10 module: share of its proteins kept in its best match at powers 8, 12 and 14.",
  "Per construction setting: modules and their leave-one-person-out stability; chosen marks ours.",
  "Per module used: median best Jaccard over 16 leave-one-person-out refits, share re-forming."
)
write_workbook(sheets, holds, file.path(out, "module_building.xlsx"), inputs, paths)
```
